label: General aftercare teaching after laparoscopic cholecystectomy and medication-reconciliation prompts. Reference material for the discharging team, not patient-specific orders. Sentinel never decides a dose, a restart or a stop.
sources: SAGES patient information: Laparoscopic gallbladder removal (cholecystectomy).
American College of Surgeons patient education: Cholecystectomy, surgical removal of the gallbladder.
ERAS Society guidelines for perioperative care (general principles of early feeding and mobilisation).

general.text: Walking from the day of surgery is usual; heavy lifting is usually limited for a few weeks, as the surgeon advises.
Most patients return to a normal diet as tolerated; some find smaller, lower-fat meals easier at first.
Small port-site incisions are kept clean and dry as instructed; dressings and showering follow the discharge sheet.
Port-site and shoulder-tip pain from the gas used in laparoscopy are common in the first days.
A follow-up visit or call with the surgical team is usually arranged in the first weeks.
Patients are usually told to report fever, yellowing of the skin or eyes, worsening abdominal pain or swelling, persistent vomiting, or redness or discharge at a wound.

anticoagulant.decision: Restart timing of the anticoagulant, and any bridging, for the surgical team to decide.

antiplatelet.decision: Restart timing of the antiplatelet for the surgical team to decide.

antihypertensive.decision: Whether and when to resume the blood-pressure medicine, for the discharging team to decide.

statin.decision: Whether to resume the home statin, for the discharging team to decide.

antibiotic.decision: Whether antibiotics continue after surgery and for how long, for the surgical team to decide.

diabetes.decision: Diabetes medicine plan around eating again, for the discharging team to decide.

default_decision: Resume, change or stop: for the discharging team to decide.
allergy_prompt: Recorded allergy or intolerance to keep in view when prescribing pain relief and other discharge medicines.
